root_cause: Existing hourly Janitor holds authorized GitHub repository write operations but does not use any GitHub Actions cache, while workflow trigger defaults can grant cache read/write access unnecessarily.

observed_evidence.privileged_actions: actions: write; contents: write; pull-requests: write; issues: write

failed_approaches: Treat a privileged non-caching job as needing inherited cache write tokens
Relax provider, Required or CodeQL controls to speed up CI
Broaden security changes across unrelated active PRs
fix: Set official GitHub Actions jobs.janitor.cache-mode: none, preventing both cache restore and save in the existing privileged non-caching Janitor. Retain exact one hourly schedule and existing cleanups/observations.
prevention_rule: Cache token permissions are least-privilege per job. An existing non-caching privileged repository janitor must not receive cache restore/save tokens. If future code needs cache, it requires independent trust review, security tests and exact-head protected merge, not an unattended privilege upgrade.

invariants: cache-mode none only for noncaching Janitor job
one Janitor job and workflow concurrency only
Required and CodeQL remain mandatory for release
real native Janitor postmerge run needed to prove provider accepts workflow
no performance speedup claim from cache-token change

terminal_rule: Exact immutable head Required, hygiene, CodeQL; native protected merge; GitHub main readback, Skill Projection, one existing Janitor executed from protected merged SHA; issue #4661 remains open for performance SLO.
